# Whallm 1.1.14-dev.2
Development prerelease. Changes since v1.1.14-dev.1. Select **Settings → Updates → Dev** to receive dev updates; the stable channel remains on v1.1.13.
## Qwen thinking limits
- Both Qwen3.8-Flash-Next and Swift1.5-Qwen3.8-Flash-Next now support an optional thinking limit. At the limit, the engine closes the thinking block and continues answering or making tool calls within the same request. - In **Model → Advanced Settings**, **Max tokens** is now **Total output limit**. Enable **Limit thinking** to set **Thinking limit**. Thinking, its closing marker, answers and tool calls all count toward the total output limit. - Chat, Responses and Completions APIs accept `think_budget`. Omit it to use the App/catalog default, use `null` to disable it for one request, or use `0` to end an open thinking block immediately. Other models reject a non-null budget. - Leave at least two output tokens beyond the thinking budget, and substantially more for useful answers. For example, `think_budget: 8192` with `max_tokens: 16384` leaves up to 8,191 answer tokens after the closing marker. API output limits override the App default. - MTP remains available and verification stops at the thinking boundary. The closing marker is included in token usage and prompt-cache history. Requests with insufficient context space are rejected rather than silently consuming the reserved answer space. - The budget is off by default. Existing settings and total output limits are preserved. Built-in throughput tests ignore the thinking budget.
## Qwen MTP scheduling
- The shared Qwen Native engine overlaps shared-expert computation with routing and required expert reads during 2–6-row MTP verification. No new setting is needed; single-token decoding, prefill and the draft layer keep their existing schedules. - The change preserves the arithmetic and does not prefetch guessed experts. A prior short Swift-only M2 Max experiment observed about 2.15% faster decoding overall. This is limited evidence, not a general speed guarantee; other models, Macs and long contexts have not been validated for this release.
## Upgrade and validation limits
- Quit the old App and restart with this build. No model redownload or settings reset is required. Enable the thinking limit explicitly if wanted, and ensure client-supplied output limits leave enough room for an answer. - Fixed-output tests cover the 8,192-token boundary, MTP on/off, cancellation, cache continuation, image-prefill handling, API streaming and tool calls. They do not establish real-model answer or tool quality. - Prior short real Swift-model checks cover forced thinking transitions with MTP on/off, repeat generation and state-file round trips. M2 Max checks also compare verification logits and state against the preceding schedule. These are not broad quality validation, full Qwen FP8 or real-image validation, or an 8,192-token remote Mho session test. - Forcing thinking to end does not guarantee a correct or complete answer. This remains a dev build; MiMo remains a preview, and the server handles one generation request at a time. - See [the usage reference](https://github.com/yanun0323/Whallm/blob/v1.1.14-dev.2/docs/usage.md) for the API contract and examples.

# Whallm 1.1.13
Changes since v1.1.12.
## Native engine for both Qwen models
- Qwen3.8-Flash-Next and Swift1.5-Qwen3.8-Flash-Next now run on the bundled C++ and Metal engine instead of MLX. - Existing model downloads, display names, API model IDs and Aliases stay unchanged. Both models support text, still images, MTP and Prompt Cache. - **Size the expert cache automatically** uses the memory available when a model loads, up to 8,192 slots. Turn it off to choose a fixed cache size. - New or reset settings enable automatic expert cache sizing, MTP and **Use 8-bit resident weights**. Saved generation, read-worker, MTP and 8-bit choices are retained. - Advanced Settings no longer shows MLX-only controls or a separate MTP expert cache size for these models.
## Model settings and API
- **Context window** sets the maximum combined input and output length for each request, within the model's supported limit. Requests that exceed it return `context_length_exceeded`. - `GET /v1/models` includes each model's context window and capabilities in its `data` entries. - The model list shows newer models first and no longer clips the available rows into a short inner list. - Throughput durations use units appropriate to their length.
## Upgrade notes
- Quit the old App before opening this version. Model weights do not need to be downloaded again. - MLX Prompt Cache files are not reused by the Native engine; prompts are processed again as needed. Native output can differ from MLX output. - The two temporary `-native` preview model IDs have been removed. If you used them, switch to `qwen3.8-flash-next-fp8` or `swift1.5-qwen3.8-flash-next-mxfp4`. - Custom Qwen runtime configurations must leave MLX-only options at their defaults; other values are rejected. The App handles this automatically. - Clients reading the former top-level `models` or `object` fields from `GET /v1/models` must use the `data` array instead.
## Validation and limits
- 767 Python tests ran with one skipped and no failures; 199 Swift tests ran with four skipped and no failures. All 24 release-script tests passed. - Local App and ZIP checks passed for signatures, bundled model files, and startup in English, Simplified Chinese and Traditional Chinese without access to the build folder or Swift localization bundle. - Prior Native checks on M2 Max covered short text, Chat, Responses, streaming and images for both models. Broad quality, performance and M5 validation remain incomplete. Earlier MLX benchmarks do not describe this engine.
Requires Apple Silicon and macOS 15 or later. Model weights are downloaded separately. Distribution builds exclude local-only debug and Dry run features.
[Full changelog](https://github.com/yanun0323/Whallm/compare/v1.1.12...v1.1.13)
